description: We are three motivated students who love space and are eager to build something transformative. Our computer science background would surely be helpful.
summary:
Our project consists of an all-round tool that helps farmers recover and prevent failed harvests. 

CropStory treats a crop incident, such as a lost harvest, yellowing leaves or a dry spell, as a case to investigate.
The farmer marks the field on a map that protects their privacy and records the crop history and symptoms. 
CropStory then pulls NASA data for that place and period: NASA POWER climate records compared against the previous ten years, GPM IMERG rainfall and HLS satellite vegetation observations. It builds a timeline of events and keeps several possible explanations open instead of naming one cause. 
Each explanation is linked to peer-reviewed studies with verified DOIs. It also lists the field measurements that would reduce the remaining uncertainty. 
To prevent the next failure, farmers enter their priorities and constraints and compare at least three crop rotation options. 
Agronomists can be invited to review the case, and the whole investigation can be exported as a reproducible report.

This matters because farmers rarely get a clear explanation of why a harvest failed, so the same losses happen again. Free NASA observations and open science give them answers they can check and act on.
details:
CropStory turns a crop failure into a case to investigate. A farmer records their fields, crop history and symptoms, and chooses how precisely each field's location is stored.

The app then gathers NASA data for that place and period: NASA POWER rainfall and temperature anomalies compared with the previous ten years, GPM IMERG satellite rainfall and HLS vegetation (NDVI) from Landsat and Sentinel-2. These feed a season timeline where users weigh rival explanations against scientific papers found through OpenAlex and verified with Crossref. The app also suggests which local measurements would settle the question. To prevent the next failure, users compare at least three crop rotations against their own constraints and priorities, invite agronomists to review the case and export a report in English or Spanish.


The main benefit is an explanation farmers can check, since every number shows its source, resolution and limitations. Free NASA data becomes usable without technical skills. Our goal is to help small and mid-sized farms without an agronomist on call avoid repeating the same losses.


We built it with Python, FastAPI and PostgreSQL on the backend, React and TypeScript on the frontend, and Docker and GitHub Actions for testing and releases. A Raspberry Pi is the demo server. We used AI coding assistants (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex), with team members reviewing their work.


CropStory is creative because it works like an accident investigation instead of giving a single score or forecast. It keeps several explanations open and treats uncertainty as useful information.
